memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, "Go, worship the Lord. Even your women and children may go with you; only leave your flocks and herds behind." But Moses said, "You must allow us to have sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the Lord our God."" - Exodus 10:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh's final offer is his most generous yet. Take the children. Take everyone. Just leave your flocks and herds behind.

It sounds reasonable. But Moses sees it instantly: the flocks were what they would sacrifice. Worship without offerings is not worship. Pharaoh was offering them a religion that cost nothing.

That is the most common counterfeit of all. Attend, sing, believe — but let it never touch your wallet, your calendar, your ambitions or your plans. Keep the herds in Egypt.

David refused this bargain when someone offered him free land and oxen for a sacrifice. He said he would not offer to God something that cost him nothing (2 Sam 24:24).

Notice also that Pharaoh is still trying to keep leverage. Property left in Egypt is a rope back to Egypt. What we refuse to surrender still owns a piece of us.

Costless worship is Pharaoh's religion, not God's.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is my worship actually costing me?
2. What have I kept in Egypt that still has a hold on me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I do not want a faith that costs me nothing. Take my time, my resources and my plans, and use them for Your glory. Amen.
